change: The package bundles the published RC12 DLL ZIP in place of RC11's rc11-docs2 ZIP. The client manifest pins it (dll_zip: file, URL, SHA256) and its DLL by dll/rc12.json; the packager, the package checker and CI refuse any other ZIP. The welcome dialog names RC12 and, for setups updated from an earlier build, the one-time Import DLL ZIP step. A client update keeps the release already selected: the BC250 screen imports the bundled ZIP only when no release is selected.
real_payload_scope: Actual OptiScaler payload and the RC12 ZIP through the --real harness mode: install and repeat update in flat, nested and Unreal-style layouts. The executable was a synthetic x64 PE header; DLL loading was not re-run (RC11 loading checks: optiscaler-client-2.json).

first_setup.scope: Packaged application in a throwaway Fedora container with /home linked to var/home and HOME=/home/<user>, Xvfb display, real hash-pinned upstream downloads, one synthetic game added manually
first_setup.fresh: pass: dependencies prepared in about 28 s; the install screen selected 4.0.0-rc12 (DLL 4b0df277...) and installed it into the game
first_setup.update_from_bc250_5: pass: after bc250.5 installed RC11, bc250.6 showed the import hint and kept 4.0.0-rc11-docs2 selected; Import DLL ZIP with the bundled ZIP selected 4.0.0-rc12 and the update replaced the DLL with the game INI unchanged

scope: Bundled DLL ZIP and its pins. Installation engine, link refusal, cache tools and dependency pins are bc250.5's, so the bc250.3 deployment evidence still applies. Rendering evidence for the bundled DLL: portable-dll-rc12.json. No new gameplay or rendering claim.
